name: Tanjong
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: Glottolog entry retired (merged into Kanowit); no references at all listed, no description of stress located

sources.citation: Blust, Robert & Alexander D. Smith. 2014. A bibliography of the languages of Borneo (and Madagascar). Phillips, ME: Borneo Research Council.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliographic record only, but decisive for the list of works to obtain: 'Osman, Nor Hisham. 1995. Kajian sistem bunyi bahasa Tanjong. DB 39.11: 964-971. Keywords: 1. shorter descriptive study, 2. Sarawak, 3. Malay.' (DB = Dewan Bahasa). Also notes Blust 1970 used Tanjong data comparatively. No other Tanjong-specific description listed.

sources.citation: Smith, Alexander D. 2017. The Languages of Borneo: A comprehensive classification. PhD diss., University of Hawai'i at Manoa.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Primary Tanjung data ('Tanjung, near Kapit town, upper Rejang, Sarawak'); sec. 2.3.2: Kanowit 'is mutually intelligible with Tanjung, which is spoken even farther in the interior'. Melanau section is historical phonology only; transcriptions carry no stress marks; no stress remark for Tanjung or any Melanau variety. SILENT.

sources.citation: Rahim Aman, Norfazila Ab. Hamid & Shahidi A.H. 2015. Rekonstruksi vokal dan diftong bahasa Melanau Purba. GEMA Online Journal of Language Studies 15(1): 189-206.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Uses Tanjong (TJG) reflexes in a Proto-Melanau vowel/diphthong reconstruction; 'praakhir/akhir' refer to syllable position only. SILENT on stress.

sources.citation: Rensch, Calvin R. 2012. Melanau and the Languages of Central Sarawak. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2012-011. Dallas: SIL International.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Summarises Chou 2002's phonologies of 11 Melanau varieties including Tanjong (TG): e/o only in Kanowit-Tanjong, s and h in all positions, only alveolar trill in Tanjong, no vowel breaking in the river dialects; Kanowit-Tanjong 82% cognate. a full-text search for stress/accent/tekanan: no hits. SILENT on stress.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Change Request 2007-235: adopted merge [tnj] Tanjung into [kxn], renamed 'Melanau, Kanowit-Tanjung' (Dave Moody, Cal Rensch, SIL-MLB; adopted 2008-01-14).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Administrative only; merges on Chou 2002's 82% lexical similarity; sources named are Chou 2002 (Proto-Melanau MA thesis, UKM) and Zaini Ozea 1989 (SMJ 40: 231-250). Nothing on phonology or stress.

sources.citation: Blust, Robert. 2018. 101 Problems and Solutions in Historical Linguistics: A Workbook. Edinburgh: Edinburgh University Press. Sound Change Problem 8 (Mukah Melanau), Background.

sources.citation: Norfazila Ab. Hamid. 2017? Rekonstruksi dan pengelompokan bahasa Melanau (PhD thesis, UKM) and related UKM-group papers using Tanjong (TJG) data (Rahim et al. 2015; Norfazila et al. 2023)
